differentiators.observation: One command, `snapback doctor --json`, gives a six-boundary installed-product qualification (launch, bundle load, query, mutation, live subscription, shutdown) with stable codes and an independent build stamp — stronger than any install verification the 0102-era competitor arms had.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: doctor must keep exercising all six boundaries against the packaged binary users actually receive, never degrade to a launch-only probe.

differentiators.observation: The publication ledger permits a full third-party byte audit: tarball sha256/sha1/sha512 and the live registry dist all triple-match, and the served binary's build stamp equals the ledger revision.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: every future closure version must retain a committed ledger with per-package registrySha256/shasum/integrity and runtimeBinarySha256.

differentiators.observation: The dev supervisor's machine-readable lifecycle (snapback.dev.v1 events + dev.ready.json descriptor) plus stdin-close stop made a scripted start/inspect/stop trivially reliable — no log parsing, no polling loops against prose.
differentiators.mustNotRegress: the ready-descriptor contract and the generated-and-loaded event remain the packaged lifecycle protocol.

differentiators.observation: The scaffolded template ships its own acceptance suite, and the live one proves zero-leak disposal (stores/consumers/subscriptions/leases/timers/listeners all 0) and empty server subscriptions after dispose.
